title: Over 2,300 Indian Sikh Pilgrims Mark Guru Nanak's 557th Birthday in Pakistan
excerpt: More than 5,000 worshippers attended the main ceremony at Gurdwara Janam Asthan in Nankana Sahib on Tuesday, as the Indian jatha's pilgrimage continues to Panja Sahib, Kartarpur and Lahore before the December 1 return.
body:
• More than 5,000 worshippers attended the main ceremony for Guru Nanak's 557th birth anniversary at Gurdwara Janam Asthan in Nankana Sahib, Pakistan, on Tuesday, according to the Associated Press.
  • A total of 2,339 Sikh pilgrims from India crossed the Wagah border for the celebrations, the Evacuee Trust Property Board (ETPB) said; Pakistan issued visas to more than 3,000 Indian Sikhs for the occasion.
  • The pilgrims' route continues to Gurdwara Sacha Sauda and Panja Sahib, then Kartarpur on November 27 and Lahore on November 29-30, returning to India via Wagah on December 1.
  • The Kartarpur Corridor, suspended by India in May 2025, remains closed; Pakistan's minorities minister renewed calls at the ceremony for India to reopen it.

Thousands of Sikh pilgrims from India gathered at Nankana Sahib in Pakistan's Punjab province on Tuesday for the main ceremony marking the 557th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism, according to the Associated Press. More than 5,000 worshippers attended ceremonies at the shrine in the town where Guru Nanak was born, according to the Associated Press.

The Indian pilgrims had crossed into Pakistan through the Wagah border on Sunday. According to the Evacuee Trust Property Board (ETPB), which manages Sikh and Hindu shrines in Pakistan, 2,339 pilgrims arrived for the festivities, and a government statement cited by AP said Pakistan had issued visas to more than 3,000 Indian Sikhs. The group was received at the border by ETPB Chairman Qamar Zaman, Secretary Nasir Mushtaq and Sardar Ramesh Singh Arora, Punjab's minister for minorities and president of the Pakistan Sikh Gurdwara Prabandhak Committee, according to The Diplomatic Insight. The ETPB opened currency-exchange facilities at the crossing and issued identity cards and bus tickets on the spot before the pilgrims left for Nankana Sahib in three convoys.

"The ETPB opened currency-exchange facilities at the crossing and issued identity cards and bus tickets on the spot before the pilgrims left for Nankana Sahib in three convoys."

Three days of celebrations at the birthplace

The celebrations at Gurdwara Janam Asthan ran from November 22 to the main ceremony on Tuesday, November 24, and included the Bhog and Akhand Path Sahib rituals followed by a Nagar Kirtan procession carrying the Guru Granth Sahib. Organisers expected more than 20,000 Sikh devotees from Pakistan and abroad across the festivities. A two-member consular team from the High Commission of India in Islamabad joined the pilgrims at Nankana Sahib to coordinate the conduct of the yatra, IANS reported.

The journey continues

The visit does not end at Nankana Sahib. The pilgrims were scheduled to visit Gurdwara Sacha Sauda in Farooqabad on Wednesday, November 25, and stay at Gurdwara Panja Sahib in Hassan Abdal, before reaching Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur on November 27 and touring historic gurdwaras in Lahore on November 29 and 30. The group returns to India by road through Wagah on December 1.

A closed corridor in the background

The pilgrimage took place while the Kartarpur Corridor — the visa-free route, subject to permit arrangements, that links Indian pilgrims directly to Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur — remains suspended. India halted movement through the corridor in May 2025 amid military tensions between the two countries. At the celebrations, Arora called on India to reopen the corridor. For now, visits like this one, made on visas through Wagah, are the route available to Indian devotees travelling to Guru Nanak's birthplace.
